headings.title: Definition and scope of statutory employee
headings.reviewNote: Defines employee under contract of hire, appointment, or election, including executive officers, minors, and dependents (except as provided in section 287.200), while excluding owner-operators leased to for-hire motor carriers and persons performing services for board, lodging, aid, or sustenance from religious, charitable, or relief organizations.

headings.title: Definition of compensable accident and event
headings.reviewNote: Defines accident as an unexpected traumatic event or unusual strain producing objective symptoms from a specific event during a single work shift.

headings.title: Definition of compensable injury and causation
headings.reviewNote: Defines injury arising out of employment, requiring accident to be the prevailing factor in medical condition and disability, and excluding idiopathic conditions.

headings.title: Definition of death within three hundred weeks
headings.reviewNote: Defines death as resulting from violent effects of accident within three hundred weeks, exempting occupational diseases from this time limit.

headings.title: Noncompensability of commute and premises doctrine
headings.reviewNote: Bars compensation for commute injuries in company-owned or subsidized automobiles and abrogates the extension of premises doctrine for property not owned or controlled by the employer.

headings.title: Definition of total disability for employment
headings.reviewNote: Defines total disability as inability to return to any employment rather than merely the previous job.

headings.title: References to commission and insurance director
headings.reviewNote: Construes commission as the labor and industrial relations commission and director as head of the department of commerce and insurance.

headings.title: Reference to division of workers' compensation
headings.reviewNote: Defines division as the division of workers' compensation within the department of labor and industrial relations.

headings.title: Definition of minor and applicable computation
headings.reviewNote: Defines minor as person under eighteen years of age while preserving section 287.250 wage computation provisions.

headings.title: Legislative abrogation of prior judicial interpretations
headings.reviewNote: Expresses legislative intent to reject and abrogate earlier case law interpretations of accident, occupational disease, and course of employment.

headings.title: Occupational diseases due to toxic exposure
headings.reviewNote: Restricts occupational diseases due to toxic exposure exclusively to listed diseases including mesothelioma, asbestosis, silicosis, and acute myelogenous leukemia.

headings.title: Definition of maximum medical improvement point
headings.reviewNote: Defines maximum medical improvement as the point where an injured worker's medical condition stabilizes and cannot reasonably improve.

entries.reviewSummary: Core definitions of employee, accident, injury, total disability, toxic exposures, and maximum medical improvement with legislative abrogation of prior precedent.

headings.title: Coverage of sheriffs and deputy sheriffs
headings.reviewNote: Includes sheriffs and deputy sheriffs as employees and counties as employers under workers' compensation law.

headings.title: Mandatory county workers' compensation insurance coverage
headings.reviewNote: Requires each county to provide licensed workers' compensation insurance, or permits a city also recognized as a county to maintain sufficient self-insurance coverage so all sheriffs and deputy sheriffs are covered.

headings.title: Average earnings of sheriffs and deputy sheriffs
headings.reviewNote: Defines average earnings for a sheriff or deputy sheriff as annual salary or fourteen dollars per day, whichever is greater.

headings.title: Limitation of county liability to workers' compensation
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that coverage of sheriffs and deputies creates no county tort liability beyond statutory workers' compensation duties.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory workers' compensation coverage for sheriffs and deputy sheriffs, county insurance obligations, wage computation, and tort liability protections.

headings.title: Definition of employer and employee thresholds
headings.reviewNote: Defines employer to include government entities, corporations, partnerships, individuals, and employers with five or more employees or one construction employee.

headings.title: Inclusion of insurers and group self-insurers
headings.reviewNote: Provides that any statutory reference to an employer includes the employer's insurer or group self-insurer.

entries.reviewSummary: Statutory definition of employer, employee threshold requirements for commercial and construction operations, and inclusion of insurers.

headings.title: Elective coverage for partners and sole proprietors
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes partners and sole proprietors to individually elect workers' compensation protection for themselves by procuring insurance policies.

headings.title: Extension of elective coverage to employees
headings.reviewNote: Extends elective coverage of partners or sole proprietors to include their otherwise ineligible employees.

headings.title: Application of law to small employers
headings.reviewNote: Applies general compensation provisions to employers electing coverage, including employers with fewer than five employees.

headings.title: Direct liability of insurance underwriting carriers
headings.reviewNote: Imposes direct and primary liability on insurers underwriting optional partner or sole proprietor coverage.

headings.title: Legislative intent regarding optional insurance coverage
headings.reviewNote: Expresses legislative intent for optional coverage and waives technical employer-employee status requirements to effectuate coverage.

headings.title: Coverage and withdrawal of family member employees
headings.reviewNote: Applies chapter to family member employees within the third degree of affinity or consanguinity unless withdrawn by listing them on a valid policy using a department-prescribed form or by written notice to a group self-insurer.

entries.reviewSummary: Elective workers' compensation coverage for partners and sole proprietors, employee extension, small employer rules, and family member withdrawal procedures.

headings.title: Limited liability company member coverage and rejection
headings.reviewNote: Beginning January 1, 1997, requires insurers to cover nonmember LLC employees and LLC members while permitting members to individually reject coverage or prospectively rescind rejection on department forms.

headings.title: S corporation shareholder rejection and rescission election
headings.reviewNote: Beginning January 1, 2018, permits S corporation shareholders holding at least forty percent interest to individually elect to reject coverage or prospectively rescind a prior rejection by written notice.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory coverage and individual rejection election rules for limited liability company members and substantial S corporation shareholders.

headings.title: Statutory employer liability for contract premises work
headings.reviewNote: Deems persons contracting for work on their premises in the usual course of business to be statutory employers liable to contractors and employees.

headings.title: Exemption for owners erecting or altering improvements
headings.reviewNote: Exempts premise owners from statutory employer status for improvement erection, demolition, or repair, making the independent contractor the employer.

headings.title: Primary and secondary liability between contractors
headings.reviewNote: Establishes primary liability on immediate employers and secondary liability on upstream contractors with recovery rights, except no such employer is liable if the employee was insured by an immediate or intermediate employer.

headings.title: Exemption for motor carrier and owner-operator
headings.reviewNote: Exempts relationships between certified commercial-zone motor carriers and independent owner-operators from statutory employer liability.

entries.reviewSummary: Statutory employer liability for contracted premises work, construction owner exemptions, contractor order of liability, and motor carrier exceptions.

headings.title: Proof of coverage for construction contractor licenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires cities and counties issuing construction contractor licenses to require a certificate of workers' compensation insurance or division-developed exemption affidavit, without any duty to investigate.

headings.title: License denial for failure to furnish proof
headings.reviewNote: Mandates denial of a construction contractor license for noncompliance with subsection 1 until the contractor furnishes a certificate of insurance.

headings.title: Unlawful fraudulent information by contractors
headings.reviewNote: Declares it unlawful, pursuant to section 287.128, for any contractor to provide fraudulent information under this section.

headings.title: No city or county liability for licensing
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in this section creates or constitutes liability or a cause of action against a city or county regarding license issuance.

entries.reviewSummary: Local business licensing requirements for construction contractors, proof of workers' compensation coverage, license denial, and local government immunity.

headings.title: Conclusive presumption of occupational disease hazard exposure
headings.reviewNote: Establishes conclusive presumption of occupational disease exposure for employment in an occupation with disease hazard for any length of time.

headings.title: Liability of last employer exposing employee
headings.reviewNote: Imposes sole compensation liability on the last employer in whose employment the employee was exposed to the disease hazard prior to disability.

headings.title: Accrual of statute of limitations for exposure
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the statute of limitations under section 287.430 does not begin to run until an occupational disease injury becomes reasonably discoverable and apparent, except industrial noise hearing loss accrues upon eligibility to file under section 287.197.

entries.reviewSummary: Presumption of exposure to occupational disease hazards, last employer liability rule, and commencement of the limitations period.

headings.title: Statutory definition of compensable occupational disease
headings.reviewNote: Defines occupational disease arising out of and in the course of employment and excludes ordinary diseases of life unless incident to occupational disease.

headings.title: Prevailing factor causation standard for disease
headings.reviewNote: Requires occupational exposure to be the prevailing factor causing medical condition and disability, excluding aging and normal day-to-day deterioration.

headings.title: Repetitive motion recognized as occupational disease
headings.reviewNote: Recognizes repetitive motion injury as compensable occupational disease only if workplace exposure was prevailing factor causing disability.

headings.title: Definition of loss of hearing disease
headings.reviewNote: Defines industrial noise hearing loss as occupational disease caused by prolonged exposure to harmful noise capable of producing deafness.

headings.title: Definition of compensable radiation disability disease
headings.reviewNote: Defines radiation disability as occupational disease caused by direct contact or exposure to radioactive substances, radium, or X-rays.

headings.title: Occupational disease coverage for emergency responders
headings.reviewNote: Provides that respiratory, hypotension, hypertension, cardiovascular, carcinoma, and psychological stress conditions of certified paid firefighters, police officers, or peace officers may be recognized as occupational diseases if a direct causal relationship is established.

headings.title: Coverage for contagious or communicable diseases
headings.reviewNote: Extends occupational disease coverage to employees exposed to and contracting contagious or communicable diseases in the course of employment.

headings.title: Prior employer liability for repetitive motion
headings.reviewNote: Assigns liability to the immediate prior employer if repetitive motion exposure with the current employer lasted less than three months and prior employer exposure was the prevailing factor.

headings.title: Posttraumatic stress disorder coverage for first responders
headings.reviewNote: Recognizes posttraumatic stress disorder under DSM-5 as compensable occupational disease for diagnosed first responders without requiring physical injury.

entries.reviewSummary: Comprehensive occupational disease definitions, prevailing factor standard, repetitive motion rules, emergency responder presumptions, and PTSD coverage.

headings.title: Employments and occupations exempt from chapter
headings.reviewNote: Exempts farm labor, private domestic servants, federal-definition qualified real estate agents and direct sellers, certain confined inmates and mental health residents (unless competitively hired), unpaid 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(19) volunteers (except under section 287.243), and amateur youth sports officials.

headings.title: Election and withdrawal of voluntary coverage
headings.reviewNote: Permits exempt employers to elect coverage by purchasing insurance policies and provides procedures for withdrawal by cancellation or notice.

headings.title: Insurer filing of policy issuance memoranda
headings.reviewNote: Requires authorized insurance companies to file policy issuance, renewal, and cancellation memoranda with the division.

headings.title: Family farm corporation officers and exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Exempts family members and officers of family farm corporations from mandatory coverage unless coverage is elected by board resolution.

headings.title: Withdrawal by corporations with two owner-employees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes corporations with no more than two owners who are sole employees to withdraw from coverage by filing notice with the division.

entries.reviewSummary: Exempt occupations and employments, procedures for voluntary election and withdrawal, insurer filings, and family farm and small corporation exemptions.

headings.title: Exemption for cases covered by federal law
headings.reviewNote: Applies this chapter to all cases within its provisions except those exclusively covered by any federal law.

headings.title: Extraterritorial application and localized employment injuries
headings.reviewNote: Applies chapter to injuries and occupational diseases in Missouri, out-of-state under a Missouri employment contract unless the contract provides otherwise, and out-of-state where employment was principally localized in Missouri within thirteen calendar weeks.

entries.reviewSummary: Statutory scope and extraterritorial application of Missouri workers' compensation law to injuries within and outside the state.

headings.title: Exclusive employer liability and employee immunity
headings.reviewNote: Imposes no-fault liability on employers, grants co-employee immunity absent affirmative negligent acts, and includes unprovoked assaults.

headings.title: Exclusivity of statutory rights and remedies
headings.reviewNote: Declares statutory workers' compensation rights and remedies exclusive of all common law claims for employees, spouses, and heirs.

headings.title: Bar on intentional self-inflicted injury claims
headings.reviewNote: Bars compensation for intentional self-inflicted injuries and assigns the burden of proof to the contesting employer.

headings.title: Increased compensation for employer statutory violations
headings.reviewNote: Increases compensation and death benefits by fifteen percent when injury is caused by employer failure to comply with statutes or lawful orders.

headings.title: Benefit reduction for employee safety violations
headings.reviewNote: Reduces compensation and death benefits by twenty-five to fifty percent for employee failure to obey known safety rules or use provided safety devices.

headings.title: Benefit reduction or forfeiture for alcohol or drugs
headings.reviewNote: Reduces benefits by fifty percent for drug rule violations, forfeits benefits if intoxication proximately caused injury, and sets testing presumptions.

headings.title: Forfeiture for voluntary recreational activity participation
headings.reviewNote: Forfeits compensation for injuries sustained in voluntary recreational activities unless directly ordered, compensated, or caused by known premises hazards.

headings.title: Standards for compensable work-related mental stress
headings.reviewNote: Requires work-related stress causing mental injury to be demonstrated by objective standards and actual events to be extraordinary and unusual.

headings.title: Exclusion of good-faith employer personnel actions
headings.reviewNote: Excludes mental injuries resulting from good-faith disciplinary actions, job evaluations, transfers, demotions, layoffs, or terminations.

headings.title: Protection of firefighter psychological stress claims
headings.reviewNote: Preserves psychological stress benefits for firefighters under section 287.067 notwithstanding mental injury restrictions.

entries.reviewSummary: Employer liability exclusivity, safety rule penalties, alcohol and substance forfeiture, recreational activity bars, and mental stress injury requirements.

headings.title: Mandatory insurer safety engineering and management program
headings.reviewNote: Requires workers' compensation insurance carriers to establish and provide comprehensive safety engineering and management services upon employer request.

headings.title: Safety program certification, review, and data reporting
headings.reviewNote: Requires director certification and at least annual review of insurer safety programs, permits contracting with private safety companies, mandates annual loss-impact data collection, and requires reporting provided services to the division.

headings.title: Division written notice of available safety programs
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to notify employers in writing of available public or private worker safety programs upon initial or new carrier coverage unless notice was given in the prior twelve months.

headings.title: Registry of certified safety consultants and engineers
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to maintain a public registry of safety consultants and safety engineers certified by the department.

entries.reviewSummary: Insurers' obligations to provide certified workplace safety engineering programs, annual evaluations, employer notices, and consultant registries.

headings.title: Mandatory employer posting of workers' compensation notice
headings.reviewNote: Beginning January 1, 1993, requires employers to post or provide written notice of workers' compensation coverage, thirty-day injury reporting deadlines, insurer or self-insured contacts, division contacts, and fraud warnings.

headings.title: Division preparation and carrier distribution of notice
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to develop and publish workplace notices and requires insurance carriers to furnish notices to insured employers within thirty days.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties for willful failure to post
headings.reviewNote: Classifies willful failure to post required workers' compensation notices as a class A misdemeanor punishable by fine or imprisonment.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory posting and distribution of workplace workers' compensation notices, carrier distribution obligations, and misdemeanor penalties.

headings.title: Unlawful presentation of false compensation claims
headings.reviewNote: Makes it unlawful to knowingly present or cause to be presented any false or fraudulent claim for workers' compensation benefits.

headings.title: Fraudulent refusal of insurer to pay obligations
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits insurers and self-insurers from knowingly and intentionally refusing to comply with indisputable compensation obligations with intent to defraud.

headings.title: Prohibited fraudulent practices and conspiracy acts
headings.reviewNote: Outlines unlawful fraudulent acts including multiple claims, conspiracy, health benefit fraud, and false statements to discourage claims or deceive investigators.

headings.title: Criminal penalties and fines for fraud violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies subsection 1 or 2 violations as class E felonies with fines up to ten thousand dollars or double fraud value, subsection 3 violations as class A misdemeanors with fines up to ten thousand dollars, and repeat violations as class D felonies.

headings.title: Unlawful preparation of invalid insurance certificates
headings.reviewNote: Classifies preparing or providing an invalid certificate of insurance as a class E felony with a fine up to ten thousand dollars or double the fraud value, whichever is greater.

headings.title: Misrepresentation of facts for lower insurance rates
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowing misrepresentation of any fact to obtain workers' compensation insurance below the proper rate as a class A misdemeanor, or a class E felony for repeat violations.

headings.title: Criminal penalties for failure to insure liability
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowing employer failure to insure liability as a class A misdemeanor with a penalty up to three times annual premium or fifty thousand dollars, whichever is greater, and repeat violations as a class E felony.

headings.title: Filing and prosecution of fraud complaints
headings.reviewNote: Permits filing fraud or noncompliance complaints with a division legal advisor for fraud unit investigation, optional director referral to and prosecution by the attorney general, workers' compensation fund cost payment and fine deposit, and restitution to defrauded persons.

headings.title: Confidentiality of fraud unit investigation records
headings.reviewNote: Deems fraud unit investigative records confidential and exempt from chapter 610, while allowing release to local, state, or federal law enforcement or agencies conducting an investigation upon written request.

headings.title: Creation of fraud and noncompliance administrative unit
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a dedicated fraud and noncompliance administrative unit within the division to investigate violations and noncompliance.

headings.title: Three-year statute of limitations for prosecutions
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a three-year statute of limitations for prosecuting workers' compensation fraud running from discovery by an aggrieved party or prosecutor.

headings.title: Annual attorney general fraud prosecution report
headings.reviewNote: Requires the attorney general by January 1, 2006, and annually thereafter, to report cases filed and prosecuted by county, fines and penalties levied and received, and prosecution costs to the division and general assembly.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibitions against workers' compensation fraud and noncompliance, criminal penalties, division fraud unit operations, and enforcement procedures.

headings.title: Health care provider fraudulent billing practices defined
headings.reviewNote: Defines fraudulent billing practices by health care providers including unbundling, upcoding, exploding diagnostic tests, and duplicating claims.

headings.title: Department investigative subpoenas and evidence collection
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department of commerce and insurance to administer oaths, subpoena witnesses and records, and collect evidence in billing fraud probes.

headings.title: Out-of-state inspection of billing records
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to inspect out-of-state records and coordinate with state and out-of-state regulatory officials.

headings.title: Criminal penalties and fines for false billing
headings.reviewNote: Classifies fraudulent billing as a class A misdemeanor with fines up to twenty thousand dollars, enhanced to class E felony for repeat violations.

entries.reviewSummary: Definitions of fraudulent health care billing practices, department investigatory and subpoena powers, and criminal misdemeanor and felony penalties.

headings.title: Certification program for managed care organizations
headings.reviewNote: Directs department of commerce and insurance to establish a program to certify managed care organizations providing workers' compensation services.

headings.title: Certification criteria and annual recertification applications
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to promulgate managed care organization approval criteria covering services, geography, staffing, provider access, oversight, peer and utilization review, dispute resolution, and case management, and requires annual recertification filings thirty days before the anniversary.

headings.title: Fee reimbursement rules and voluntary alternative agreements
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to promulgate rules on insurer reimbursement of managed care fees and operational coordination, while permitting insurers and managed care organizations to enter voluntary alternative fee agreements exempt from those rules.

headings.title: Deemed compliance for organizations certified before 1993
headings.reviewNote: Deems any managed care organization previously certified by the director prior to August 28, 1993, to have met the statutory criteria of this section.

headings.title: Division review of managed care treatment decisions
headings.reviewNote: Subjects recommended or provided medical services to division review upon application after internal utilization review and appeal, allowing modification of payment decisions only upon a showing they were unreasonable, arbitrary, or capricious.

entries.reviewSummary: Certification and annual recertification of workers' compensation managed care organizations, fee reimbursement and operational coordination rules, pre-1993 grandfathering, and division review of medical care decisions.

headings.title: Employer duty to provide medical treatment services
headings.reviewNote: Requires employers to provide medical, surgical, and hospital care, regulates provider communication, and establishes travel distance expense limits.

headings.title: Division authority to order change of physician
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes division or commission to order change of health care provider if employee life, health, or recovery is endangered.

headings.title: Regulation of medical fees and charges
headings.reviewNote: Requires medical fees to be fair and reasonable, limited to usual private payor rates, and vests regulatory jurisdiction in division and commission.

headings.title: Administrative procedures for medical fee disputes
headings.reviewNote: Establishes administrative procedures and strict filing deadlines of one or two years for resolving medical provider fee disputes.

headings.title: Forfeiture for unreasonable refusal of treatment
headings.reviewNote: Bars compensation if employee unreasonably refuses medical or surgical treatment that presents inconsiderable risk relative to injury.

headings.title: Admissibility of treating physician testimony
headings.reviewNote: Declares testimony of treating physicians and chiropractic physicians admissible in workers' compensation proceedings.

headings.title: Inspection and admissibility of hospital records
headings.reviewNote: Requires hospitals and medical providers to permit record copying and makes certified medical records admissible in evidence.

headings.title: Provision of prostheses and claim reactivation
headings.reviewNote: Permits the division or commission to require employers to furnish artificial limbs, joints, eyes, or braces for life when relieving permanent injury effects, and directs claim reactivation procedures upon good cause for life-threatening surgical procedures or prosthetic needs.

headings.title: Treatment by prayer or spiritual means
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes employee treatment by spiritual means or prayer provided the employer does not object to such treatment.

headings.title: Employer right to select treating provider
headings.reviewNote: Vests the right to select treating physicians, surgeons, and healthcare providers in the employer within scope of medical licensure.

headings.title: Health care provider financial interest disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Requires healthcare providers to disclose in writing financial interests in referral institutions to patients, employers, and insurers.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for failure to disclose
headings.reviewNote: Classifies failure of a healthcare provider to disclose referral financial interests as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Prohibition against provider billing injured employee
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits medical providers from balance billing injured workers upon receipt of written claim notice and provides civil damages for violations.

headings.title: Use of accumulated leave for medical visits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes employers to allow or require employees to use accumulated paid leave to attend medical treatment or evaluations during work time.

entries.reviewSummary: Comprehensive medical treatment obligations, employer provider selection, medical fee regulations, prostheses furnishing, and balance billing protections.

headings.title: Purpose and administration of physical rehabilitation
headings.reviewNote: Establishes statutory purpose of physical rehabilitation to restore injured workers to self-support under division administration.

headings.title: Investigation and certification of rehabilitation facilities
headings.reviewNote: Directs division to study rehabilitation, inspect facilities, and certify qualified physical rehabilitation institutions and physicians.

headings.title: Second injury fund rehabilitation weekly benefits
headings.reviewNote: Directs requisition of forty dollars per week from the second injury fund during accepted physical rehabilitation for up to twenty weeks, except additional periods may be authorized by special division order in unusual cases.

headings.title: Employer selection of certified rehabilitation facility
headings.reviewNote: Grants employers or insurers the right to select qualified certified facilities and physicians for offered rehabilitation.

headings.title: Dispute resolution procedure for physical rehabilitation
headings.reviewNote: Establishes division hearing procedures and order authority for resolving disagreements regarding physical rehabilitation necessity.

headings.title: Authority to order employee rehabilitation transportation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to order employer or insurer to furnish transportation for injured employee to rehabilitation facilities.

headings.title: Scope of physical rehabilitation services included
headings.reviewNote: Defines physical rehabilitation to include medical, surgical, and hospital restoration services under section 287.140.

headings.title: Judicial appeals of physical rehabilitation orders
headings.reviewNote: Provides for appeals of division physical rehabilitation orders to the appellate court in the same manner as compensation cases.

entries.reviewSummary: Physical rehabilitation administration, facility certification, second injury fund weekly benefit stipends, dispute hearings, and judicial appeals.

headings.title: Written application for rehabilitation practitioner certification
headings.reviewNote: Requires individuals seeking status as rehabilitation practitioners to submit written requests to the division for qualification review and certification.

headings.title: Certification requirements for independent rehabilitation practitioners
headings.reviewNote: Requires independent rehabilitation practitioners entering the vocational rehabilitation workers' compensation field after January 1, 1990, to obtain national board certification or meet division qualifications.

headings.title: Certification requirements for rehabilitation service providers
headings.reviewNote: Requires vocational rehabilitation providers to submit written certification requests to the division for qualification and registration.

entries.reviewSummary: Certification and registration procedures and qualification standards for vocational rehabilitation practitioners and service provider organizations.

headings.title: Authorization for employee vocational rehabilitation services
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes injured employees sustaining severe injuries to receive vocational rehabilitation services upon employer and insurer approval.

headings.title: Statutory duties of director regarding vocational rehabilitation
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to maintain provider registries, report annual results and costs, review and disapprove plans within fourteen days, monitor ongoing compliance, and appoint qualified rehabilitation monitors; source footnote notes that '7' appears in original rolls where subsection 2(3) prints '5'.

entries.reviewSummary: Eligibility authorization for employee vocational rehabilitation and statutory duties of the director in administering rehabilitation plans and registries.

headings.title: Determination of loss of gainful employment
headings.reviewNote: Requires employer assessment of loss of suitable gainful employment within one hundred twenty days and provider assessment within ninety days.

headings.title: Serious injuries qualifying for vocational rehabilitation
headings.reviewNote: Defines severe injuries qualifying for rehabilitation including amputations, spinal cord paralysis, severe burns, and head or sensory injuries.

headings.title: Director notification to employer of severe injury
headings.reviewNote: Directs director to immediately notify employer upon receipt of medical reports detailing severe injuries qualifying for rehabilitation.

headings.title: Duration and cost limits of rehabilitation plans
headings.reviewNote: Limits initial plans to twenty-six weeks with employer-only twenty-six-week extension and caps implementation and retraining costs at five thousand dollars without division approval, excluding medical treatment, evaluation, and provider fees.

headings.title: Board, lodging, and travel expense provisions
headings.reviewNote: Requires employer payment of reasonable board, lodging, and travel costs when rehabilitation requires temporary residence away from home.

entries.reviewSummary: Assessment of loss of gainful employment, severe qualifying injury criteria, plan duration and cost caps, and travel and lodging provisions.

headings.title: Payment of temporary disability during rehabilitation
headings.reviewNote: Mandates payment of temporary total or partial disability benefits throughout rehabilitation until maximum medical improvement or return to work.

headings.title: Adjudication of permanent disability barred during rehabilitation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits establishing, determining, or adjudicating permanent disability while the injured employee is actively participating in rehabilitation.

headings.title: Benefit reduction for refusal of rehabilitation services
headings.reviewNote: Imposes a fifty percent reduction in weekly disability benefits for employee refusal to accept rehabilitation services or assessments.

entries.reviewSummary: Temporary disability benefit payments during rehabilitation, bar on adjudicating permanency, and fifty percent benefit reduction for refusal.

headings.title: Employer subrogation rights against liable third parties
headings.reviewNote: Subrogates employers to the rights of employees or dependents against liable third parties and allows recovery of full third-party damages.

headings.title: Employer subrogation lien in wrongful death recoveries
headings.reviewNote: Grants employers a statutory subrogation lien on third-party wrongful death judgments or settlements with comparative fault adjustments.

headings.title: Apportionment of third-party recovery and expenses
headings.reviewNote: Governs apportionment of third-party recoveries between employer and employee after deduction of proportionate expenses and reasonable attorney fees.

headings.title: Subrogation of second injury fund recoveries
headings.reviewNote: Subrogates the second injury fund to employee rights against third parties to the extent of physical rehabilitation benefits paid.

headings.title: Immunity of construction design professionals from liability
headings.reviewNote: Immunizes construction design professionals and their employees from liability for employer safety standard failures unless safety responsibility is assumed by contract, excluding negligent preparation of design plans or specifications.

headings.title: Prohibition of subrogation waivers in construction contracts
headings.reviewNote: Declares contractual subrogation waivers in construction contracts void as against public policy and regulates insurer recovery credits.

headings.title: Exception to employer subrogation for toxic exposure
headings.reviewNote: Bars employer subrogation against liable third parties for occupational diseases due to toxic exposure arising from work for the employer; source footnote notes 'employer's' appears as a typographical error for 'employee's' in original rolls.

entries.reviewSummary: Employer and second injury fund subrogation rights, third-party recovery apportionment, design professional immunity, and toxic exposure exceptions.

headings.title: Waiting period and retroactive payment conditions
headings.reviewNote: Except as provided in section 287.140, bars compensation for the first three business days of disability unless disability lasts longer than fourteen days, in which case the first three days are paid retroactively.

headings.title: Payment schedule and direct employer payments
headings.reviewNote: Requires benefit payments at least biweekly and permits direct employer payments with insurer indemnification and reimbursement rules for noncompensable claims.

headings.title: Simple interest on delayed benefit payments
headings.reviewNote: Imposes ten percent simple interest per annum on undisputed benefit payments delayed more than thirty days and contested awards.

headings.title: Applicable rules governing compensation payments
headings.reviewNote: Directs that compensation shall be payable in accordance with the rules in sections 287.170, 287.180, 287.190, 287.200, 287.240, and 287.250.

headings.title: Prohibition against employer credit for wages
headings.reviewNote: Bars employers from taking credit for wages or pay benefits paid to the employee or dependents on account of injury or death, except as provided in section 287.270.

entries.reviewSummary: Three-day disability waiting period, biweekly payment schedules, late payment interest, and prohibition against employer wage credits.

headings.title: Temporary total disability computation and duration
headings.reviewNote: Caps temporary total disability at four hundred weeks at sixty-six and two-thirds percent of average earnings up to statutory maximums.

headings.title: Method of temporary total disability payments
headings.reviewNote: Requires temporary total disability payments directly to claimant by check, electronic transfer, or to claimant's attorney upon request.

headings.title: Disqualification during receipt of unemployment compensation
headings.reviewNote: Disqualifies employees from receiving temporary total disability during periods when unemployment compensation is sought and received.

headings.title: Disqualification for employee post-injury misconduct
headings.reviewNote: Bars temporary total and temporary partial disability benefits if terminated from post-injury employment for post-injury misconduct, excluding injury absence unless a physician certifies the employee can work with restrictions.

headings.title: Forfeiture upon voluntary separation with available work
headings.reviewNote: Bars temporary total and partial disability when an employee voluntarily separates while the employer has medically accommodated work available.

entries.reviewSummary: Computation and duration of temporary total disability, direct payment methods, and disqualifications for unemployment or misconduct.

headings.title: Temporary partial disability computation and limits
headings.reviewNote: Caps temporary partial disability at one hundred weeks at sixty-six and two-thirds percent of pre-injury and post-injury wage differences.

headings.title: Method of temporary partial disability payments
headings.reviewNote: Requires temporary partial disability payments to the claimant by check, other negotiable instrument, electronic transfer, or other manner authorized by the claimant.

entries.reviewSummary: Temporary partial disability wage-loss computation, maximum one-hundred-week duration, and authorized payment delivery methods.

headings.title: Permanent partial disability schedule of losses
headings.reviewNote: Establishes statutory schedule of weeks of compensation for specified permanent partial amputations and sensory losses.

headings.title: Ten percent increase for total scheduled loss
headings.reviewNote: Increases scheduled compensation weeks by ten percent when disability in items (1) through (29) is total by severance or complete loss of use.

headings.title: Proportionate compensation for unscheduled permanent injuries
headings.reviewNote: Provides proportionate compensation up to four hundred weeks for unscheduled permanent injuries and partial loss of member use.

headings.title: Additional compensation for permanent disfigurement
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes up to forty weeks of additional compensation for serious and permanent head, neck, hand, or arm disfigurement.

headings.title: Weekly rate computation for permanent partial disability
headings.reviewNote: Specifies weekly permanent partial disability rate computation based on average earnings and statutory percentages of state average wage.

headings.title: Objective medical findings and age reduction
headings.reviewNote: Establishes continuation presumption for prior ratings, requires objective physician certifications, and reduces awards for aging.

entries.reviewSummary: Permanent partial disability schedule of losses, unscheduled injuries, disfigurement awards, physician certification, and preexisting aging offsets.

headings.title: Compensable frequency range for industrial noise
headings.reviewNote: Confines compensable industrial noise hearing losses to frequencies of five hundred, one thousand, and two thousand cycles per second, excluding losses above two thousand cycles per second.

headings.title: Hearing loss measurement frequencies and decibels
headings.reviewNote: Requires pure tone air conduction audiometric instruments and establishes decibel loss thresholds based on ANSI standards.

headings.title: Permanent partial disability weeks for deafness
headings.reviewNote: Provides forty-nine weeks of compensation for total deafness in one ear and one hundred eighty weeks for total binaural deafness.

headings.title: Average decibel loss and percentage calculation
headings.reviewNote: Establishes mathematical formula converting decibel losses exceeding twenty-six decibels into percentage disability allowances.

headings.title: Calculation formula for binaural hearing loss
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes weighted formula multiplying better ear disability by five, adding poorer ear percentage, and dividing by six.

headings.title: Age deduction for nonoccupational hearing loss
headings.reviewNote: Requires deducting one-half decibel from total average decibel loss for each year of employee age over forty at last exposure to industrial noise for nonoccupational hearing loss.

headings.title: Separation from noisy work before filing
headings.reviewNote: Bars filing an occupational deafness claim until after one month's separation from noisy work for the last exposing employer, establishing the last day of separation as the date of disability.

headings.title: Employer liability for occupational hearing loss
headings.reviewNote: Imposes liability for entire occupational deafness on contributing employer absent proof of preexisting established hearing loss.

headings.title: Hearing aid improvement excluded from calculation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits considering hearing improvement resulting from use of hearing aids when calculating compensable hearing loss.

entries.reviewSummary: Occupational deafness measurement, ANSI decibel standards, binaural loss calculation formulas, age deductions, and hearing aid exclusions.

headings.title: Lifetime compensation for permanent total disability
headings.reviewNote: Mandates weekly lifetime compensation for permanent total disability from maximum medical improvement date up to statutory wage caps.

headings.title: Accrued benefits payable upon employee death
headings.reviewNote: Provides that unaccrued permanent total disability compensation terminates upon employee death and does not survive to dependents or estate.

headings.title: Suspension of benefits upon work restoration
headings.reviewNote: Mandates suspension of permanent total disability life payments while an employee is restored to regular work or its equivalent by glasses, prosthetics, or rehabilitation, while keeping the file open for review.

headings.title: Toxic exposure benefits and enhanced compensation
headings.reviewNote: For toxic exposure claims filed on or after January 1, 2014, provides permanent total benefits after exhausting two hundred percent SAWW for one hundred weeks (non-mesothelioma) or optional three hundred percent SAWW for two hundred twelve weeks (mesothelioma, with paragraphs (a) and (b) of subdivision (3) expiring December 31, 2038).

headings.title: Limitation on combined asbestosis and mesothelioma benefits
headings.reviewNote: Caps total benefits for an employee who receives asbestosis benefits under subsection 4(2) and later receives a mesothelioma award so total recovery does not exceed mesothelioma-only benefits.

entries.reviewSummary: Permanent total disability lifetime benefits, death termination rules, work-restoration suspensions, toxic exposure and mesothelioma enhancements, and asbestosis-mesothelioma offset cap.

headings.title: Mandatory employee submission to physical examination
headings.reviewNote: Requires employee submission to reasonable medical examinations requested by the employer, insurer, commission, division, administrative law judge, or attorney general for the second injury fund, forfeiting compensation during unjustified refusal or obstruction.

headings.title: Appointment and report of impartial physician
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission, division, or administrative law judge when deemed necessary to appoint an impartial examining physician, regulates fees and party copies, and makes the report admissible if all parties have reasonable access.

headings.title: Seven-day deadline for exchanging medical reports
headings.reviewNote: Requires exchange of medical reports at least seven days prior to hearing or deposition under penalty of witness preclusion.

headings.title: Division and commission access to reports
headings.reviewNote: Directs that copies of all medical reports be furnished to administrative law judges, the division, or commission upon request.

headings.title: Definition of complete medical report contents
headings.reviewNote: Defines complete medical report to include qualifications, history, complaints, diagnostic findings, diagnosis, prognosis, and rating.

headings.title: Treating physician duty to provide report
headings.reviewNote: Requires treating physicians upon party request to furnish a rating, complete medical report, and complete clinical records at the expense of the party selecting the physician.

headings.title: Admissibility of complete medical reports
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes admission of complete medical reports sixty days before hearing with deposition cross-examination procedures.

headings.title: Admissibility of coroner inquest proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Deems certified coroner inquest records admissible in workers' compensation death claim proceedings with right of cross-examination.

headings.title: Authority to order postmortem examination
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes division or commission in extraordinary cases to order postmortem examinations and body exhumation.

entries.reviewSummary: Medical examinations of injured workers, report exchange rules, admissibility of complete reports and coroner records, and autopsy orders.

headings.title: Creation and administration of second injury fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates Second Injury Fund in state treasury administered by state treasurer upon requisitions by division director.

headings.title: Pre-2014 preexisting permanent disability compensation rules
headings.reviewNote: Governs pre-2014 claims combining preexisting permanent partial disability with subsequent injury, assigning fund excess liability.

headings.title: Post-2014 permanent total disability fund liability
headings.reviewNote: Restricts post-2014 fund liability strictly to permanent total disability meeting statutory threshold criteria and bars partial claims.

headings.title: State treasurer defense and legal costs
headings.reviewNote: Names the state treasurer as defending party with compromise settlement authority upon attorney general advice and consent, requires assistant attorneys general for claims filed on or after July 1, 1994, and makes legal expenses contingent on annual appropriations effective July 1, 1993.

headings.title: Concurrent temporary disabilities in same employment
headings.reviewNote: Provides that concurrent temporary disabilities in same employment are compensable only for longest and largest paying disability.

headings.title: Consecutive permanent partial disability compensation payments
headings.reviewNote: Requires consecutive permanent partial disability payments for multiple injuries in same employment.

headings.title: Second injury fund payments for uninsured employers
headings.reviewNote: Permits withdrawing fund moneys for medical and death expenses from pre-January 1, 2014 injuries or deaths of uninsured employers' employees, grants treasurer employer defenses and civil recovery reimbursement, and directs attorney general suits against uninsured employers.

headings.title: Annual actuarial study of fund solvency
headings.reviewNote: Requires an annual actuarial solvency study of the second injury fund, with the first completed prior to July 1, 2014, paid from the division support fund.

headings.title: Financial records and claims data compilation
headings.reviewNote: Directs division director to maintain fund financial data, compile multiple-employment claim data, and receive attorney general reports.

headings.title: Public inspection of second injury claims
headings.reviewNote: Declares all claims for fees and expenses filed against the second injury fund to be open public records.

headings.title: Pre-2014 multiple employment wage loss claims
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes wage loss claims against the second injury fund for pre-January 1, 2014 injuries involving concurrent multiple employers, leaving medical costs with the employer where the injury occurred.

headings.title: Bar on fund claims filed out-of-state
headings.reviewNote: Bars second injury fund compensation if claimant files workers' compensation claim in another state with jurisdiction.

headings.title: Suspension of life payments upon employment
headings.reviewNote: Suspends second injury fund life payments when employee obtains gainful employment or self-employment under division means test.

headings.title: Review and appeal of fund awards
headings.reviewNote: Subjects all awards affecting the second injury fund to statutory administrative review and judicial appeal provisions.

headings.title: Statutory priority order for fund liabilities
headings.reviewNote: Sets payment priority for fund liabilities when a positive balance exists: legal defense, permanent total awards, permanent partial awards, pre-July 1, 2012 uninsured medical expenses, and interest on unpaid awards.

headings.title: Adjusted interest rates on fund awards
headings.reviewNote: Sets post-award interest rates on second injury fund claims at adjusted director of revenue rate or five percent minimum.

headings.title: Priority death and ongoing medical benefits
headings.reviewNote: Permits the division to pay pre-January 1, 2014 uninsured death benefits and ongoing (but not past) future medical expenses ahead of subsection 15 priority tiers.

entries.reviewSummary: Second injury fund operations, post-2014 permanent total restrictions, uninsured employer coverage, priority tiers, and actuarial reviews.

headings.title: Creation of mesothelioma risk management fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri Mesothelioma Risk Management Fund as a body corporate and politic with board powers necessary to carry out section purposes.

headings.title: Definitions for mesothelioma risk management fund
headings.reviewNote: Defines board and fund for purposes of this section.

headings.title: Employer participation and payment of awards
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any employer to participate in the fund and use funds collected under this section to pay mesothelioma awards against a member employer.

headings.title: Annual contribution assessments for member employers
headings.reviewNote: Requires participating employers to pay annual contributions determined by the board relating to insurer rates, equates participation to insurance or self-insurance, and designates fund moneys for mesothelioma claims and administrative legal expenses.

headings.title: Cap on fund claim payments
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits paying any amount from the fund in excess of the statutory cap in section 287.200(4)(3)(a) for claims arising out of any award.

headings.title: Board issuance of benefit payments
headings.reviewNote: Directs board benefit payments, relieves the board of liability for years without employer contribution, imposes a five-year bar on resuming after discontinuation, and holds nonpaying employers liable under section 287.200(4)(3)(b) and for ongoing fund benefits; source footnote notes 'fail' appears in original rolls.

headings.title: Department provision of administrative staff
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of labor to provide staff reimbursed annually by contract unless the board determines otherwise, disclaims state liability, and declares fund moneys are not state money.

headings.title: Employer notice of claims to board
headings.reviewNote: Requires member employers to notify board of trustees within seven working days of learning of any potential claim.

headings.title: Authority to contract with insurance agents
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes board to contract with independent insurance agents to accept contributions and market coverages.

headings.title: Establishment of board of trustees composition
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a five-member board consisting of the director of the department of labor and four governor-appointed, senate-confirmed officers or employees of participating employers serving staggered four-year terms.

headings.title: Trustee immunity from personal civil liability
headings.reviewNote: Immunizes trustees from personal liability for claims made against the fund or member employers.

headings.title: Election of board chairman and duties
headings.reviewNote: Directs the board to elect a chairman to preside over meetings and perform other duties required by board action.

headings.title: Appointment and duties of vice chairman
headings.reviewNote: Directs chairman to appoint vice chairman to perform duties in absence of chairman.

headings.title: Appointment of secretary and custody of records
headings.reviewNote: Directs the board to appoint a secretary who has charge of fund offices and records subject to board direction.

headings.title: Meeting location and calling procedures
headings.reviewNote: Requires board meetings in Jefferson City upon call of chairman or agreement of three trustees.

headings.title: Quorum and official board action requirements
headings.reviewNote: Establishes three trustees as a quorum and bases official board action on a majority vote of the trustees present.

headings.title: Trustee reimbursement for actual expenses
headings.reviewNote: Provides trustees serve without compensation but receive reimbursement from fund for necessary expenses.

headings.title: Member employer employee service on board
headings.reviewNote: Deems board duties performed by employees of member employers as regular work hours without loss of compensation.

headings.title: Complete record of all board proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board to keep a complete record of all its proceedings.

headings.title: Annual operating statement and financial report
headings.reviewNote: Requires an annual statement of operations, income, disbursements, and financial condition as of July first to be delivered to the governor and made readily available to public entities.

headings.title: General administrative responsibility of the board
headings.reviewNote: Vests general administration and operational responsibility of the fund in the board of trustees.

headings.title: Prescribing rules, coverages, forms, and rates
headings.reviewNote: Directs the board to determine and prescribe all rules, regulations, coverages, forms, and rates to carry out this section.

headings.title: Exclusive board jurisdiction over fund assets
headings.reviewNote: Vests exclusive jurisdiction and control over fund moneys, investments, and property in the board of trustees.

headings.title: Prohibition against trustee personal profit
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any trustee or staff member from receiving any gain or profit from fund moneys or transactions.

headings.title: Forfeiture of office for accepting gratuities
headings.reviewNote: Mandates forfeiture of office for any trustee or staff member accepting any gratuity or compensation to influence investment or fund operations.

headings.title: Authority to purchase insurance or reinsurance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the board to purchase insurance or reinsurance covering participating member employer liabilities, with costs considered in determining member contributions.

headings.title: Risk management and safety inspection assistance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes board to assist member employers in assessing and reducing workplace toxic exposure risks.

headings.title: Establishment of special fund bank account
headings.reviewNote: Requires establishment and maintenance of Missouri mesothelioma risk management fund account for deposits.

headings.title: Secretary collection and deposit of moneys
headings.reviewNote: Directs payment of fund moneys to the secretary for deposit in banks or trust companies holding section 30.270 collateral, with a required corporate surety bond.

headings.title: Prudent investment of fund property assets
headings.reviewNote: Directs safe investment of fund assets for reasonable return and permits investments allowed for Missouri casualty insurance companies' capital, reserve, and surplus funds.

headings.title: Deficiency assessments on member employers
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board to assess members, including withdrawn members from the assessment year, for proportionate shares of unpaid claims if contributions are insufficient, retroactively to fund creation.

headings.title: Selection of professional and actuarial consultants
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the board to employ or contract with technical advisors experienced in underwriting, accounting, claims servicing, and ratemaking, or to call upon the director of commerce and insurance.

headings.title: Nonalteration of member employer legal liabilities
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in this section broadens or restricts member employer liability beyond this section or abolishes or waives available legal defenses; source footnote notes 'sections' appears in original rolls.

headings.title: Premium refunds for excess operating reserves
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes board to refund excess operating reserves to member employers at fiscal year-end.

entries.reviewSummary: Creation, governance, funding, employer contributions, claims administration, investments, and assessments of the Missouri Mesothelioma Risk Management Fund.

headings.title: Accrued compensation payable upon employee death
headings.reviewNote: Provides that employee death terminates disability but accrued unpaid compensation remains payable to dependents or estate without administration.

headings.title: Unpaid unaccrued permanent partial disability benefits
headings.reviewNote: Directs that unpaid unaccrued permanent partial disability under section 287.190 passes to surviving dependents if death is unrelated to injury.

headings.title: Legislative abrogation of Schoemehl decision
headings.reviewNote: Expresses legislative intent to reject and abrogate the holding in Schoemehl v. Treasurer regarding survival of permanent total disability.

entries.reviewSummary: Employee death as termination of disability, payment of accrued compensation, and legislative abrogation of Schoemehl decision.

headings.title: Title of Line of Duty Compensation Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates section as the Line of Duty Compensation Act.

headings.title: Definitions for Line of Duty Compensation
headings.reviewNote: Defines air ambulance crew, child, emergency medical technician, firefighter, killed in line of duty, and public safety officer.

headings.title: Two-year claim deadline and payment amount
headings.reviewNote: Requires claims to be filed within two years of death and provides one hundred thousand dollars in compensation, subject to appropriation, for deaths occurring on or after June 19, 2009.

headings.title: Order of distribution among surviving family
headings.reviewNote: Establishes statutory order of distribution to surviving spouse, children, designated beneficiaries, parents, or adult children.

headings.title: Claim filing requirements and division investigation
headings.reviewNote: Requires detailed claim applications and directs the division of workers' compensation to investigate and substantiate facts.

headings.title: Line of duty compensation additional to other benefits
headings.reviewNote: Provides line of duty compensation is in addition to, and not exclusive of, other pension or death benefits.

headings.title: Subrogation bar and exemption from execution
headings.reviewNote: Bars employer and insurer subrogation against benefits and exempts compensation from debt execution except attorney fees.

headings.title: Right to administrative hearing and review
headings.reviewNote: Establishes right to administrative hearing before an administrative law judge and commission review for aggrieved claimants.

headings.title: Sunset and termination dates of program
headings.reviewNote: Establishes automatic program sunset date of December 31, 2031, with final termination on September 1, 2032.

headings.title: Nonapplicability of other workers' compensation provisions
headings.reviewNote: Exempts line of duty compensation claims from other general provisions of chapter 287 unless expressly referenced.

headings.title: Creation of Line of Duty Compensation Fund
headings.reviewNote: Establishes dedicated nonreverting Line of Duty Compensation Fund in state treasury to pay approved claims.

headings.title: Division rulemaking authority and severability provisions
headings.reviewNote: Grants division authority to promulgate administrative rules subject to nonseverability provisions of chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Line of Duty Compensation Act, eligible public safety officer definitions, benefit distribution orders, and dedicated state treasury fund.

headings.title: Definitions for volunteer firefighter premium grants
headings.reviewNote: Defines association, state fire marshal, volunteer firefighter, and voluntary critical illness benefits pool; source footnote notes section 320.270 was repealed by H.B. 57, 1987.

headings.title: Grant applications for insurance and critical illness pools
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes volunteer fire associations and critical illness pools to apply to the state fire marshal for premium grants.

headings.title: Grant disbursement schedule based on claims
headings.reviewNote: Subject to appropriations, permits the state fire marshal to disburse grants from five hundred to two thousand dollars to applying volunteer fire protection associations based on the number of volunteer firefighters receiving benefits for fire or underwater recovery claims in the preceding calendar year.

headings.title: Restriction of grant funds to premiums
headings.reviewNote: Restricts use of grant funds solely to paying workers' compensation insurance premiums or voluntary critical illness pool costs.

entries.reviewSummary: State fire marshal grant program funding workers' compensation insurance premiums and critical illness pools for volunteer firefighters.

headings.title: Computation of employee average weekly wage
headings.reviewNote: Establishes average weekly wage formulas for weekly, monthly, yearly, and daily, hourly, or output wages (using the preceding thirteen calendar weeks), plus rules for employment under two weeks or unfixed wages.

headings.title: Inclusions and exclusions from gross wages
headings.reviewNote: Includes board, rent, housing, and lodging (unless continued during disability) and reported gratuities in wages, while excluding employer-furnished fringe benefits, helper wages, and special expense payments.

headings.title: Wage calculation for part-time employees
headings.reviewNote: Calculates benefits for part-time workers based on full-time wage rates for similar work with a minimum thirty-hour workweek base.

headings.title: Exceptional methods for determining weekly wage
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes division or commission to determine average weekly wage using exceptional methods when standard formulas cannot fairly apply.

headings.title: Apportionment for prior disability compensation recipients
headings.reviewNote: Apportions compensation for subsequent injuries where employee was already disabled and drawing compensation under this chapter.

headings.title: Wage adjustments for minors and apprentices
headings.reviewNote: Adjusts average weekly wage for workers under twenty-one or apprentices to reflect expected career earning increases up to three years.

headings.title: Additional compensation for child labor violations
headings.reviewNote: Mandates fifty percent additional compensation if employer knowingly employed a minor in violation of state child labor laws.

headings.title: Wage calculation for multiple employment situations
headings.reviewNote: Aggregates average weekly wages from multiple employments solely for temporary total or temporary partial disability under section 287.220; source footnote notes the reference to subsection 9 appears to correspond to subsection 11 after S.B. 1, 2013.

headings.title: Compromise lump sum proration over lifetime
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes compromise settlements prorating lump sum awards over claimant's life expectancy with prorated rates controlling.

entries.reviewSummary: Formulas for calculating average weekly wage, part-time and apprentice adjustments, child labor penalties, and settlement life expectancy proration.

headings.title: Compensation exemption from execution and liens
headings.reviewNote: Exempts compensation from assignment, attachment, garnishment, and execution, grants wage priority upon insolvency, and regulates attorney fees.

headings.title: Assignment and attachment for child support
headings.reviewNote: Makes compensation other than medical expenses and therapy under section 287.141 assignable and subject to attachment, garnishment, execution, and section 454.517 liens for child support obligations, with section 452.140 limiting exemptions.

entries.reviewSummary: Exemption of workers' compensation benefits from creditor claims and execution, attorney fee liens, and exception for child support collection.

headings.title: Definitions of provider and eligible person
headings.reviewNote: Defines provider and person eligible for public assistance for recovery of medical assistance payments.

headings.title: Public assistance debt due to state
headings.reviewNote: Declares public assistance payments made on behalf of injured workers for compensable injuries to be a debt due to the state.

headings.title: State lien upon employer compensation funds
headings.reviewNote: Creates a state lien on compensation funds owed by employers or insurers to satisfy public assistance debts.

headings.title: State subrogation rights to employee recoveries
headings.reviewNote: Subrogates the state to any funds owed to or received by the employee or representative for compensable injuries.

headings.title: Department actions to recover public funds
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department of social services to maintain legal actions and appeals under workers' compensation law to recover expended funds.

headings.title: Recovery of full amount of payments
headings.reviewNote: Affirms department right to recover the full amount of medical assistance paid to providers for compensable work injuries.

headings.title: Subordination of state debt to attorney fees
headings.reviewNote: Subordinates state debt solely to fee rights of injured employee's attorney without requiring state fee contributions.

headings.title: Assignment of rights upon assistance acceptance
headings.reviewNote: Deems application for and receipt of public assistance an automatic assignment of recovery rights to department of social services.

headings.title: Attorney notification to department of representation
headings.reviewNote: Requires claimant's attorney to notify department of social services upon representing client who received public assistance.

headings.title: Judicial apportionment of debt due state
headings.reviewNote: Directs the administrative law judge to apportion the debt due the state between the injured worker and employer when no agreement is reached, without reducing the total debt due the state.

entries.reviewSummary: State recovery of public assistance paid for compensable injuries, statutory liens, subrogation rights, and judicial debt apportionment.

headings.title: Mandatory insurance and individual self-insurance requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires employers to insure entire liability or self-insure, sets failure penalties, and permits common-law damage actions.

headings.title: Uniform experience rating plans for groups
headings.reviewNote: Requires qualified self-insurance employer groups to use uniform experience rating plans and remit claims history to advisory organizations.

headings.title: Discount caps for group self-insurance members
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits group self-insurers from authorizing total discounts exceeding twenty-five percent for any individual member beginning January 1, 1999, and requires uniform application based on objective quantitative factors.

headings.title: Filing of premium rates for groups
headings.reviewNote: Requires self-insured groups to file adequate premium rates based on pure premium data or top-twenty insurer averages, exempting political subdivisions self-insured on an assessment plan under section 537.620.

headings.title: Trust self-insurer initial payment requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires new trust self-insurer applicants to show proof of paying at least twenty-five percent of estimated annual premium, or for mid-year new members the lesser of three months' or balance-of-year estimated premium.

headings.title: Investment authority for surplus trust moneys
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes self-insured trusts to invest up to one hundred percent of surplus moneys in collateral approved for state deposits.

headings.title: Division findings subject to administrative review
headings.reviewNote: Provides for administrative and judicial review of division determinations regarding self-insurance authority.

headings.title: Default and security forfeiture for insolvency
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to call posted security upon insolvency or bankruptcy of a self-insured group or public sector individual employer, allows third-party administrator referral, limits liability to security proceeds, and preserves members' joint and several liability.

headings.title: Rulemaking promulgation requirements under chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Requires administrative rules promulgated under this section to comply with standard state rulemaking requirements.

headings.title: Confidentiality of self-insurance financial records
headings.reviewNote: Deems financial records submitted by self-insurers confidential and exempt from open records laws except by subpoena.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory workers' compensation insurance, individual and group self-insurance standards, rate filings, insolvency remedies, and confidentiality.

headings.title: Separate coverage for leased employee arrangements
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes requiring separate workers' compensation coverage or self-insurance for leased employees and nonleased employees.

headings.title: Rulemaking standards for employee leasing arrangements
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes administrative rules governing registration, information reporting, client experience rating, and policy auditing for leasing arrangements.

headings.title: Exclusion of temporary help service arrangements
headings.reviewNote: Excludes temporary help service arrangements addressing finite skill shortages and seasonal workloads from leasing definitions.

headings.title: Rebuttable presumption for single client leasing
headings.reviewNote: Establishes rebuttable presumption that leasing employees to only one client company is an arrangement to avoid proper contribution rates.

entries.reviewSummary: Workers' compensation coverage requirements for employee leasing arrangements, temporary help exclusions, and contribution avoidance presumptions.

headings.title: Policy approval and mandatory insurer covenants
headings.reviewNote: Requires all workers' compensation policies to be approved by insurance department and contain binding agreements to fulfill statutory obligations.

headings.title: Authorization of employer deductible insurance plans
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes optional employer deductible plans subject to insurance department approval, barring deductibles charged to employees.

headings.title: Terms of deductible agreements and reimbursements
headings.reviewNote: Regulates deductible payment terms, requiring insurers to retain ultimate claim liability and pay providers directly with employer reimbursement.

headings.title: Premium reductions and experience modification credits
headings.reviewNote: Requires approved premium reductions reflecting deductible levels and credits employer-paid deductible losses against experience modification unless the employer purchases a gross reportable deductible plan.

headings.title: Financial ability investigation for deductible plans
headings.reviewNote: Relieves insurers from offering deductibles if credit investigation reveals employer lacks financial ability to pay deductible amounts.

headings.title: Insurer duty to service and defend claims
headings.reviewNote: Directs insurers to service and defend all claims arising during the policy period including deductible amounts.

headings.title: Prohibition of retaliation for deductible claims
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits employer discrimination, harassment, or discharge of employees for filing claims that trigger deductible obligations.

headings.title: Rating organization filing of deductible plans
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes licensed rating organizations to file deductible plans on behalf of their member insurers for department approval.

headings.title: Surcharge calculations for policies with deductibles
headings.reviewNote: Bases administrative surcharges on premiums for the deductible credit portion, second injury fund surcharges on total premiums without the deductible option, and premium taxes on premiums excluding the deductible credit portion without retaliatory tax on the surcharge portion.

headings.title: Data reporting rules for deductible policies
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director of the department of commerce and insurance to specify by rule any data reporting requirements applicable to workers' compensation policies with deductible options.

entries.reviewSummary: Department approval of workers' compensation policies, employer deductible options, insurer claims servicing, and anti-retaliation protections.

headings.title: Creation and composition of review board
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Workers' Compensation Determinations Review Board within the department of commerce and insurance with five governor-appointed voting members and two nonvoting advisory members (state actuary and licensed rating organization representative).

headings.title: Review of code classifications and recalculations
headings.reviewNote: Empowers board upon employer application to review code classifications, order reclassifications, and recalculate experience modification factors.

headings.title: Board recommendations for uniform classification changes
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board to recommend changes to the uniform classification system.

headings.title: Advisory organization disclosure of classification materials
headings.reviewNote: Requires advisory organizations developing classification systems to provide development materials and scope descriptions to affected parties.

entries.reviewSummary: Workers' Compensation Determinations Review Board establishment, composition, employer classification review hearings, and modification factor audits.

headings.title: Mandatory employer report of employee injury
headings.reviewNote: Requires employers to report all injuries to carriers within five days and carriers to file complete injury reports with division within thirty days.

headings.title: Duty to return blank reporting forms
headings.reviewNote: Requires employers, insurers, employees, and dependents to promptly complete and return all inquiry forms propounded by division.

headings.title: Confidentiality of reported injury accident data
headings.reviewNote: Restricts disclosure of reported injury information to parties and their attorneys except by division or commission order or at a compensation hearing, while permitting statistical use by the division or commission.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties for failure to report
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowing failure to report accidents or filing false reports as a criminal misdemeanor punishable by fines or imprisonment.

entries.reviewSummary: Employer and insurer mandatory injury reporting timelines, information disclosure restrictions, and criminal penalties for noncompliance.

headings.title: Voluntary compromise settlements and judicial approval
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes voluntary compromise settlements after seven days from injury, requiring administrative law judge or commission approval for validity.
