headings.title: Extinguishment of death claims upon settlement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an approved compromise settlement during the employee's lifetime extinguishes all death compensation claims if it compromises a dispute on any issue other than extent of disability or compensation rate.

headings.title: Employee option for lump sum settlement
headings.reviewNote: Grants employee the option of receiving approved compromise settlement as a one-time lump sum payment.

headings.title: Compromise settlements on behalf of minors
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes parent or conservator of minor dependent to execute compromise settlement discharging employer from further liability.

headings.title: Employee entitlement to unrepresented settlement offers
headings.reviewNote: Entitles unrepresented employees to one hundred percent of written settlement offers filed with the division even after obtaining counsel.

headings.title: Definition of amount in dispute terms
headings.reviewNote: Defines amount in dispute as excess above employer written offer and clarifies offers do not constitute admissions of liability.

headings.title: Twelve-month limit for second rating acquisition
headings.reviewNote: Gives claimant twelve months from receiving employer permanent disability rating at maximum medical improvement to obtain second rating.

entries.reviewSummary: Compromise settlements of compensation claims, approval standards, lump sum options, minor dependents, and twelve-month rating limits.

headings.title: Division hearing procedure and written awards
headings.reviewNote: Governs division evidentiary hearings, requires issuance of written awards within ninety days, and mandates electronic or mail service.

headings.title: Provision of mediation services for claims
headings.reviewNote: Directs division to develop administrative rules providing mediation services to resolve claims prior to formal evidentiary hearings.

headings.title: Mediation conference procedures and mediator disqualification
headings.reviewNote: Regulates informal mediation conferences, allows production of medical records, and disqualifies mediators from hearing cases.

entries.reviewSummary: Division evidentiary hearing procedures, ninety-day award issuance, mediation conference services, and mediator trial disqualification.

headings.title: Application for commission review and filing
headings.reviewNote: Establishes twenty-day deadline for filing application for review of award with full commission, mailbox rule, and facsimile filings.

headings.title: Appeal bond requirement for uninsured employers
headings.reviewNote: Requires uninsured employers appealing awards to post an appeal bond covering full award amount as jurisdictional prerequisite.

entries.reviewSummary: Twenty-day deadline for application for review before commission, mailbox rule filing criteria, and mandatory appeal bond for uninsured employers.

headings.title: Final award conclusiveness and circuit appeal
headings.reviewNote: Deems final commission awards conclusive unless appealed within thirty days to circuit court and limits judicial review to four statutory grounds.

headings.title: Appellate procedure and priority of appeals
headings.reviewNote: Regulates appellate court procedures for circuit court appeals, transcript transmissions, and gives compensation appeals statutory precedence.

headings.title: Application restricted to pre-1980 compensation claims
headings.reviewNote: Restricts application of this section strictly to claims arising prior to August 13, 1980, with subsequent claims governed by section 287.495.

entries.reviewSummary: Circuit court appeal procedures for pre-August 13, 1980 workers' compensation awards, transcript requirements, and four grounds for reversal.

headings.title: Appellate court review of commission awards
headings.reviewNote: Establishes appellate court jurisdiction over appeals of final commission awards within thirty days and specifies four statutory grounds for reversal.

headings.title: Application to claims on or after August 13, 1980
headings.reviewNote: Applies direct appellate court review provisions to all workers' compensation disputes based on claims arising on or after August 13, 1980.

entries.reviewSummary: Appellate court review of commission final awards, venue determinations, record transcripts, and exclusive grounds for setting aside awards.

headings.title: Methods and service of statutory notice
headings.reviewNote: Deems notice properly served when sent by registered or certified mail to last known address or served like civil summons.

headings.title: Electronic transmission of official notices
headings.reviewNote: Permits the division to serve notices electronically, except unrepresented employees must receive registered or certified mail unless they consent to electronic notice, and represented employees may receive regular mail when counsel is properly notified.

entries.reviewSummary: Methods of serving official workers' compensation notices by certified mail, civil summons, or authorized electronic transmission.

headings.title: Lump sum commutation of future compensation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes division or commission to commute future compensation installments into lump sum payment based on life contingencies and best interests.

headings.title: Unusual circumstances required for award commutation
headings.reviewNote: Requires unusual circumstances to justify lump sum commutation as departure from normal periodic wage-replacement installment payments.

entries.reviewSummary: Division and commission authority to commute future compensation into lump sum payments and requirement of unusual circumstances.

headings.title: Appointment and qualifications of administrative judges
headings.reviewNote: After August 28, 2005, permits appointing up to forty full-time Missouri-licensed attorney administrative law judges and requires website publication of appointment or initial service dates.

headings.title: Retention vote schedule for administrative judges
headings.reviewNote: Establishes staggered retention votes on August 28, 2008, 2012, and 2016 and every twelve years thereafter, barring retention votes for judges receiving two or more no-confidence votes under committee audits.

headings.title: Qualifications for administrative review committee members
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits review committee members from having direct or indirect financial ties to workers' compensation insurers or practicing as comp attorneys.

headings.title: Recommendation of confidence by review committee
headings.reviewNote: Requires review committee to issue recommendations of confidence or no confidence within thirty days of each performance audit.

headings.title: Jurisdiction and powers of administrative judges
headings.reviewNote: Vests original hearing jurisdiction in administrative law judges, restricts review hearings, and allows clerical error corrections within twenty days.

headings.title: Temporary branch office assignments for judges
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes temporary assignment of administrative law judges to branch offices to ensure efficient statewide administration.

headings.title: Continuing education and professional training requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires administrative law judges to participate in ongoing continuing legal and medical training programs established by the division.

headings.title: Biennial performance audits and committee structure
headings.reviewNote: Requires biennial performance audits by a four-voting-member legislative review committee plus one nonvoting ex officio governor appointee, permitting immediate withdrawal of appointment after three or more no-confidence votes across two successive audits.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking authority under chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Requires all administrative rules promulgated under this section to comply with chapter 536 rulemaking procedures.

entries.reviewSummary: Administrative law judge appointments, qualifications, retention voting cycles, performance audit committees, and original hearing jurisdiction.

headings.title: Appointment and salaries of division personnel
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes division staff appointments and sets annual salaries beginning January 1, 2006, for chief legal counsel, administrative law judges, and judges in charge; Revisor's Note references the section 105.005 salary adjustment index in Appendix E.

headings.title: Division director salary and bipartisan appointments
headings.reviewNote: Sets minimum salary for division director and requires bipartisan selection of appointees in each classification from major political parties.

entries.reviewSummary: Appointment and salary structures for administrative law judges, legal counsel, and division personnel, with bipartisan selection mandates.

headings.title: Division offices, supplies, and traveling expenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires division offices in designated cities with permanent records in Jefferson City and reimburses verified employee travel expenses.

headings.title: Venue and hearing locations in counties
headings.reviewNote: Establishes hearing venue in county where accident occurred, adjacent county, or where contract was made or employment localized.

headings.title: Location of commission hearings on review
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes commission to hold review hearings at locations determined with due regard for convenience of the parties.

entries.reviewSummary: Location of permanent and branch division offices, traveling expense reimbursements, hearing venue rules, and commission review locations.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and electronic processes implementation
headings.reviewNote: Empowers division to make rules, implement electronic processes, strike pleadings, and enter awards against noncompliant parties.

headings.title: Retention and destruction of injury records
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes destroying uncompensated injury reports after five years and mandates storing compensable case records and exhibits for ten years.

headings.title: Rulemaking compliance under section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Requires all administrative rules promulgated under this section to comply with section 536.024.

entries.reviewSummary: Division rulemaking authority, electronic processes, default sanction powers, and document retention and destruction periods.

headings.title: Schedule of division fees for records
headings.reviewNote: Establishes statutory fee schedule for copies of records, certified documents, annual reports, and proceedings paid into support fund.

headings.title: Expenses of self-insurance financial investigations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes collecting reasonable expenses of self-insurance financial investigations from employers and exempts official records furnished to public officers.

entries.reviewSummary: Statutory fee schedule for copying and certifying division records and collection of self-insurance investigation expenses.

headings.title: Annual tax return of insurance carriers
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurance carriers and self-insurers to file verified annual tax returns of gross premiums and deposits by March first.

headings.title: Quarterly installment payments and tax reconciliation
headings.reviewNote: Requires quarterly estimated tax payments on March, June, September, and December first, with annual reconciliation and credit rules.

headings.title: Certification and collection of insurance taxes
headings.reviewNote: Directs insurance director to certify tax amounts due and revenue director to notify, assess, and collect taxes.

headings.title: Disposition of proceeds in support fund
headings.reviewNote: Directs deposit of collected tax proceeds into the fund for the support of the division of workers' compensation.

headings.title: Dedicated purpose and safeguarding of fund proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Restricts tax proceeds and interest collected under sections 287.690, 287.715, and 287.730 exclusively to relieving industrial injury victims and providing physical rehabilitation, imposing an official duty to safeguard them.

headings.title: Nonreversion of workers' compensation fund balances
headings.reviewNote: Exempts funds under sections 287.220, 287.690, 287.715, and 287.730 from section 33.080 general revenue transfer, permits the division director to direct state treasurer investments in interest-bearing accounts, and carries forward unexpended second injury fund balances.

entries.reviewSummary: Annual tax returns and quarterly payments by insurance carriers and self-insurers, tax rate certification, and support fund dedication.

headings.title: Annual surcharge for second injury fund
headings.reviewNote: Imposes an annual second injury fund surcharge on authorized self-insurers and policyholders for policies written or renewed on or after April 26, 1988, including the state and political subdivisions, excluding reinsurance or retrocessional transactions.

headings.title: Calculation and collection of annual surcharge
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division director beginning October 31, 2005, to set the annual surcharge (capped at three percent targeting one hundred ten percent of projected payments for calendar years beginning January 1, 2006), permits temporary advances from the workers' compensation fund, and bars insurer collection fees or taxes.

headings.title: Deposit of collections into second injury fund
headings.reviewNote: Mandates deposit of all surcharge amounts to the credit of the second injury fund in the state treasury.

headings.title: Quarterly payment schedule for surcharge amounts
headings.reviewNote: Requires quarterly payment of surcharges by insurers and self-insurers by the thirtieth day following each quarter.

headings.title: Penalties for failure to remit surcharge
headings.reviewNote: Imposes civil penalty of one-half of one percent on unpaid or untransferred surcharge amounts collected in summary proceedings.

headings.title: Supplemental surcharge on net insurance premiums
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division director to collect a supplemental surcharge up to one percent for calendar years 2014 through 2026, rounded up to the nearest quarter-point, expiring December 31, 2026.

headings.title: Exclusive funding source of second injury fund
headings.reviewNote: Declares funds collected under chapter 287 to be the sole funding source for the second injury fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Annual and supplemental surcharges funding the Second Injury Fund, calculation methodology, collection procedures, and statutory expiration.

headings.title: Annual administrative surcharge on deductible policies
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division director to impose an annual administrative surcharge on deductible plan policyholders for policies written or renewed on or after January 1, 2004, to fund division administration.

headings.title: Calculation basis for deductible policy surcharge
headings.reviewNote: Calculates the administrative surcharge on total premiums that would have been paid for the deductible credit portion, set at the same rate as the section 287.690 premium tax.

headings.title: Advance annual notification to insurance carriers
headings.reviewNote: Requires division to notify all workers' compensation insurers of the administrative surcharge percentage within ten days of determination.

entries.reviewSummary: Annual administrative surcharge on deductible policies funding division operations, calculation formulas, and carrier notification.

headings.title: Collection of administrative surcharge from policyholders
headings.reviewNote: Beginning January 1, 2004, directs insurers to collect the administrative surcharge with premiums without fee or commission, exempting the surcharge from taxes, licenses, or fees.

headings.title: Deposit of surcharges into administrative fund
headings.reviewNote: Requires administrative surcharges to be paid to the director of revenue and deposited into the workers' compensation administrative fund.

headings.title: Quarterly installment payment schedule for surcharges
headings.reviewNote: Requires four estimated quarterly surcharge installments on March, June, September, and December first with annual report by March first.

headings.title: Annual reconciliation and credit for overpayment
headings.reviewNote: Provides for crediting overpayments against following year's surcharge installments or cash refund if no payments due.

headings.title: Late charges for unpaid or untransferred surcharges
headings.reviewNote: Assesses a late charge of one-half of one percent on unpaid or untransferred administrative surcharges against liable policyholders or insurers, collected in a civil summary proceeding by the division director.

headings.title: Delinquent interest on unpaid administrative surcharges
headings.reviewNote: Imposes interest at one and one-half percent per month on delinquent administrative surcharges.

headings.title: Electronic filing authorization and records confidentiality
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes electronic submission of surcharge filings and deems filed surcharge information confidential and exempt from open records.

headings.title: Exemption of authorized self-insurers from surcharge
headings.reviewNote: Exempts authorized individual and group self-insurers from the provisions of this surcharge section.

entries.reviewSummary: Collection procedures for deductible plan administrative surcharges, quarterly installments, late penalties, and records confidentiality.

headings.title: Delinquent interest on unpaid insurance taxes
headings.reviewNote: Imposes interest at one and one-half percent per month on delinquent workers' compensation taxes and disputed assessments.

headings.title: Quarterly tax payments during legal contests
headings.reviewNote: Requires quarterly tax installments during tax contests based on assessed amounts, with refunds or credits for overpayments.

entries.reviewSummary: Interest rates on delinquent workers' compensation taxes and requirement of quarterly installment payments during legal contests.

headings.title: Strict construction of workers' compensation law
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that administrative law judges, legal advisors, the commission, the division, and reviewing courts strictly construe chapter provisions.

headings.title: Impartial weighing of evidence by adjudicators
headings.reviewNote: Requires adjudicators to weigh evidence impartially without giving the benefit of the doubt to any party in resolving factual conflicts.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory strict construction of workers' compensation statutes and impartial weighing of evidence without benefit of doubt.

headings.title: Religious exemption and benefit waiver application
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes employees with conscientious religious objections to public or private insurance to apply for exception from workers' compensation.

headings.title: Prescribed division form for religious waiver
headings.reviewNote: Requires religious waiver applications and supporting employer affidavits to be filed on prescribed division forms.

headings.title: Duration of religious exemption until rescinded
headings.reviewNote: Provides that granted religious exemptions remain valid until rescinded by the employee or sect requirements cease to be met.

headings.title: Prospective effect of religious benefit waiver
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that religious rejection of benefits operates prospectively from the date rescission form is received by the insurer.

entries.reviewSummary: Procedures for religious sect members to waive workers' compensation benefits, required division forms, duration, and prospective effect.

headings.title: Application for change of administrative judge
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes automatic change of administrative law judge in any hearing upon written application without alleging or proving cause.

headings.title: Timelines for filing change of judge
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing at least thirty days before the hearing or within five days of hearing setting, whichever is later, or within ten days after designation (or before hearing, whichever is earlier) if undesignated; source footnote notes 'be' appears in original rolls.

headings.title: Limitation to one change of judge
headings.reviewNote: Limits each party in a workers' compensation proceeding to one change of administrative law judge.

headings.title: Mandatory transfer and designation of judge
headings.reviewNote: Directs commission to promptly sustain timely application and designate another administrative law judge.

entries.reviewSummary: Procedures, deadlines, and single-change limitations for disqualifying and replacing administrative law judges in compensation hearings.

headings.title: Retirement qualifications for administrative law judges
headings.reviewNote: Effective August 28, 1999, sets age and service qualifications (62/12, 60/15, or 55/20) for judges and legal advisors leaving office on or after August 13, 1984, and permits crediting general assembly service for certain appointees who waive other general assembly benefits.

headings.title: Twelve-year service vesting for retirement benefits
headings.reviewNote: Vests retirement benefits upon completing twelve aggregate years of service regardless of employment status upon reaching age eligibility.

headings.title: Crediting prior state employee retirement service
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes crediting prior state employee retirement service for judges and legal advisors waiving rights under other systems.

headings.title: Special consultant status for hearing commissioners
headings.reviewNote: Appoints former administrative hearing commissioners as special consultants on retirement and aging with benefit eligibility.

entries.reviewSummary: Age and service retirement eligibility qualifications for administrative law judges and legal advisors, vesting rules, and service credits.

headings.title: Monthly payment of judge retirement benefits
headings.reviewNote: Provides retirement benefits in equal monthly installments for life equal to fifty percent of highest salary received during service.

headings.title: Exemption from execution and health deductions
headings.reviewNote: Exempts retirement benefits from execution, garnishment, attachment, and assignment except under section 104.312 or for child support or maintenance, and permits written requests for group prepaid hospital, medical, and surgical premium withholding.

headings.title: Withholding of group health insurance premiums
headings.reviewNote: Directs system executive director to withhold and pay over authorized group health insurance premiums upon written member request.

headings.title: Special consultant appointment and annual increases
headings.reviewNote: Beginning January 1, 1989, appoints retired members employed prior to August 28, 1997, as special consultants on aging receiving annual CPI-based increases between four and five percent, capped at sixty-five percent of initial benefit.

headings.title: Additional cost of living benefit increases
headings.reviewNote: Provides additional annual cost-of-living benefit increases up to five percent once initial consultant benefit increase limits are reached.

headings.title: Annual percentage increases for newer judges
headings.reviewNote: Provides annual consumer price index percentage increases up to five percent for judges first employed on or after August 28, 1997.

headings.title: Cost of living increases for survivors
headings.reviewNote: Extends annual consumer price index retirement benefit increases to surviving beneficiaries of newer judges.

headings.title: Payment from retirement fund and funding
headings.reviewNote: Directs payment of retirement compensation in monthly installments from retirement fund funded on an actuarial basis.

entries.reviewSummary: Retirement benefit calculations for administrative law judges, exemption from execution, consultant cost-of-living increases, and fund disbursements.

headings.title: Survivor benefits upon death of judge
headings.reviewNote: On and after August 13, 1984, pays immediate monthly survivor benefits equal to fifty percent of section 287.820 retirement benefits upon an active judge's or legal advisor's death, proportionally reduced if retirement rules precluded twelve years of service.

headings.title: Survivor benefits upon death of retiree
headings.reviewNote: Provides monthly survivor benefits equal to fifty percent of retirement benefits upon death of retired administrative law judge.

headings.title: Survivor benefits for vested nonretired judges
headings.reviewNote: Provides fifty percent survivor benefits upon death of former judge with twelve years of service who died before retiring.

headings.title: Successive survivor benefits for dependent beneficiaries
headings.reviewNote: Directs payment of survivor benefits to surviving eligible dependent beneficiaries upon death of surviving spouse.

entries.reviewSummary: Survivor retirement benefits payable to beneficiaries upon death of active, retired, or vested administrative law judges.

headings.title: Forfeiture of retirement benefits upon misconduct
headings.reviewNote: Bars retirement benefits to any person removed by impeachment or for misconduct, any person disbarred from practicing law, and the beneficiary of any such person.

headings.title: Forfeiture of survivor benefits for homicide
headings.reviewNote: Directs the MOSERS board to cease paying benefits to a beneficiary charged with intentionally killing the judge or legal advisor without legal excuse, terminating benefits upon conviction or resuming with back pay if not convicted.

entries.reviewSummary: Forfeiture of retirement benefits upon impeachment, misconduct removal, or disbarment, and bar on survivor benefits for homicide.

headings.title: Board administration of judge retirement system
headings.reviewNote: Vests administration of administrative law judge retirement system in MOSERS board of trustees based on law in effect at termination.

headings.title: State treasurer duties and separate accounts
headings.reviewNote: Directs commissioner of administration, state treasurer, and system secretary to maintain and disburse separate retirement accounts.

headings.title: Transfer and combination with state system
headings.reviewNote: As of April 26, 2005, transfers and combines liabilities and assets of the administrative law judge and legal advisor retirement system into MOSERS while preserving prior participants' and beneficiaries' rights.

entries.reviewSummary: MOSERS board administration of administrative law judge retirement system, state officer duties, and combination with state employee system.

headings.title: Exclusivity of judge retirement benefit plan
headings.reviewNote: Declares judge retirement plan the exclusive plan for benefits based on services as administrative law judge or legal advisor.

headings.title: Transfer of prior state retirement contributions
headings.reviewNote: Requires transferring state or division contributions made to any other retirement system on a judge's or legal advisor's behalf upon August 13, 1984, to the separate section 287.845 account.

headings.title: Nonapplicability to federal social security benefits
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that plan exclusivity provisions do not apply to benefits paid or contributions made under federal Social Security.

entries.reviewSummary: Exclusivity of administrative law judge retirement system, transfer of prior retirement contributions, and social security exceptions.

headings.title: Purchase of creditable prior military service
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes administrative law judges and legal advisors to purchase up to four years of prior active military service for retirement credit.

headings.title: Refund of military purchase to spouse
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes refund of military service purchase contributions to surviving spouse if member dies prior to retirement without survivorship benefit.

entries.reviewSummary: Procedures for purchasing creditable prior military service in judge retirement system and refund options for surviving spouses.

headings.title: Creation of private sector guaranty corporation
headings.reviewNote: Creates Missouri Private Sector Individual Self-Insurers Guaranty Corporation as not-for-profit corporation with mandatory self-insurer membership.

headings.title: Withdrawal conditions and actuarial security requirements
headings.reviewNote: Regulates member withdrawal, requiring continued liability, annual reporting, and independent actuarial opinions with security deposits.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishment of private sector individual self-insurers guaranty corporation, mandatory membership, and withdrawal conditions.

headings.title: Board of directors size and plan organization
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an eight-member board of directors, including the division director permanently, organized under the section 287.870 plan of operation.

headings.title: Initial board appointments and nonvoting division director
headings.reviewNote: Designates the division director as a permanent nonvoting board member who initially appoints seven qualified private sector self-insurer members.

headings.title: Staggered initial terms, four-year terms, and limits
headings.reviewNote: Sets staggered initial terms ending by January 1, 1995, 1996, and 1997, followed by member-recommended four-year terms with a two-consecutive-term limit.

headings.title: Board vacancies, removal for cause, and filling
headings.reviewNote: Defines vacancy triggers, permits majority-vote removal for incompetence, neglect, or malfeasance, and requires the board to fill vacancies within thirty days.

headings.title: Uncompensated board service and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the division director and board members receive no remuneration but are reimbursed for expenses incurred performing board duties.

headings.title: Selection and tenure governed by plan and rules
headings.reviewNote: Directs that all other matters regarding board member selection and tenure be set forth in the plan of operation and applicable rules and regulations.

entries.reviewSummary: Board of directors composition, nonvoting status of the division director, staggered initial and subsequent four-year terms with two-term limits, vacancy filling, expense reimbursement, and plan governance for the guaranty corporation.

headings.title: Disbursed moneys vested in corporation, not state
headings.reviewNote: Vests division-collected moneys disbursed to the corporation in the corporation, declaring them not state property and not subject to legislative or state agency appropriation.

headings.title: Dedicated use of insolvency fund moneys
headings.reviewNote: Restricts insolvency fund moneys, exclusive of reasonable board-determined administrative costs, solely to compensating employees of insolvent Missouri self-insurers and defraying fund expenses.

headings.title: Investment of fund moneys and annual audit
headings.reviewNote: Directs board investment of fund moneys with returns retained in the fund, and requires an annual independent CPA or approved audit at the division director's request.

headings.title: Confidential solvency reports to division director
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board to report to the division director on self-insurer solvency, liquidation, rehabilitation, or conservation, exempting such reports from chapter 610 public disclosure.

headings.title: Covered claim obligations and bankruptcy filing requirements
headings.reviewNote: Defines corporation liability for covered claims upon liquidation order or asset exhaustion, offsets bankruptcy proceeds, bars corporation penalties or interest, requires division notice, and bars division jurisdiction unless the claimant files and submits a certified bankruptcy proof of claim.

headings.title: Corporate powers, subrogation, contracting, and membership review
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the corporation to request revocation of self-insurer authority, sue and exercise subrogation, retain staff or third-party administrators, borrow or insure, contract, join trade associations, assist with membership reviews, issue advisory opinions, and charge examination fees.

headings.title: Division assessments, initial funding, and reassessment thresholds
headings.reviewNote: Directs division assessments capped at one million dollars aggregate and one-sixth of one percent annually, sets a six-hundred-thousand-dollar three-year initial levy and fifty-thousand-dollar pre-August 28, 1992 claim set-aside, and triggers reassessment below four hundred thousand dollars.

headings.title: Uniform assessment rate, notice, and new members
headings.reviewNote: Requires uniform percentage assessments not exceeding one-sixth of one percent of prior-year modified standard premium, at least thirty days' written notice, and plan-based assessments for newly admitted members.

headings.title: Proration of payments when funds are insufficient
headings.reviewNote: Directs proration of available funds if annual assessments and existing funds are insufficient to pay owing obligations, with unpaid balances paid when additional funds become available.

headings.title: Prohibition on state funding except assigned rights
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits allocating or paying any state funds to the corporation or its accounts except state funds accruing through assignment of an insolvent employer's rights.

headings.title: Safeguarding corporation assets for employee claims
headings.reviewNote: Requires holding all corporation moneys, property, and assets so as to advance corporate objectives and preserve moneys needed to pay claims of insolvent private self-insurers' employees.

headings.title: Vesting and reinvestment of income; dissolution trust
headings.reviewNote: Vests asset and investment income in the corporation for employee welfare without inuring to members or the division, permits reinvestment, and holds surplus income in trust for employees upon dissolution.

headings.title: Prohibition on dividends, rebates, or distributions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the corporation and insolvency fund from paying dividends, rebates, or interest or otherwise distributing income to any member.

entries.reviewSummary: Non-state status and dedicated use of insolvency fund moneys, investments and audits, confidential solvency reports, covered claim obligations and bankruptcy filings, corporate powers, assessment limits, proration, and dividend prohibition.

headings.title: Creation of insolvency fund managed by corporation
headings.reviewNote: Creates an Insolvency Fund managed by the corporation upon adoption of a plan of operation or applicable division rules under section 287.870.

headings.title: Purpose of insolvency fund after asset exhaustion
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the fund to meet obligations of insolvent members incurred during membership after exhausting all assets, bonds, escrow deposits, insurance, or reinsurance, operating under the plan of operation.

headings.title: Annual division audit of fund financial soundness
headings.reviewNote: Grants the division authority to audit the financial soundness of the insolvency fund annually.

headings.title: Division recommendations for plan of operation amendments
headings.reviewNote: Permits the division to recommend plan of operation amendments to the board to assure ongoing financial soundness and ability to meet statutory obligations.

headings.title: Actuarial and division recommendations for claim payments
headings.reviewNote: Permits an actuary on behalf of the division or appropriate division personnel to make recommendations to improve the orderly payment of claims.

entries.reviewSummary: Creation and purpose of the Insolvency Fund, annual division financial soundness audits, and division or actuarial recommendations on plan amendments and orderly claim payments.

headings.title: Submission of plan of operation
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board of directors to submit a proposed plan of operation for the corporation and insolvency fund to the division by January 1, 1993, or another agreed date.

headings.title: Purpose of plan and member fund responsibility
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the plan's purpose to authorize insolvency protection programs, make members responsible for maintaining an adequate insolvency fund, and authorize contracting with experts.

headings.title: Plan effective date and default division rules
headings.reviewNote: Makes the plan and amendments effective upon written submission to the director, and directs division rulemaking if the board fails to submit a plan within six months after August 28, 1992, or required amendments within thirty days.

headings.title: Mandatory member employer compliance with plan
headings.reviewNote: Requires all member employers to comply with the plan of operation.

headings.title: Required contents and procedures of plan
headings.reviewNote: Specifies eleven mandatory plan provisions, including power execution, asset handling, board reimbursement, claim filing and receiver notice, meetings, financial records, thirty-day appeals, board nominations, rulemaking, and division cooperation.

entries.reviewSummary: Submission deadline, purpose, effective date, default division rulemaking, mandatory member compliance, and required contents of the guaranty corporation's plan of operation.

headings.title: Mandatory division notification and information duties
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to notify the corporation of an insolvent employer within ten working days, provide annual modified standard premium statements upon board request, and establish cooperation procedures.

headings.title: Discretionary sanctions and authority of division
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes suspension of self-insurance authority, penalties, and designated servicing facilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines mandatory and discretionary oversight duties and administrative powers of the division concerning insolvent self-insurers and guaranty operations.

headings.title: Assignment of rights by benefit recipients
headings.reviewNote: Deems receipt of benefits under chapter as assignment of employee rights to corporation.

headings.title: Binding settlements and priority against insolvent assets
headings.reviewNote: Binds the receiver, liquidator, or statutory successor to corporation settlements of covered claims, grants equal court priority against insolvent employer assets, and gives claim-handling expenses liquidator expense priority.

headings.title: Periodic claim statements filed with receiver
headings.reviewNote: Requires the corporation to periodically file statements of paid covered claims and anticipated claim estimates with the receiver or liquidator to preserve rights against insolvent member assets.

entries.reviewSummary: Assignment of claimant recovery rights to the guaranty corporation, binding effect and priority of claims against insolvent employer assets, and periodic statements to receivers.

headings.title: Board duty to report hazardous member condition
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board of directors, upon majority vote determination that a member employer may be insolvent or in hazardous financial condition, to notify the division.

headings.title: Board request for division member qualification determination
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board by majority vote to request a division determination of a member's qualification within thirty days or reasonable time for good cause, keeping the request nonpublic until release.

headings.title: Division duty to report unqualified member condition
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to report to the board when it has reasonable cause to believe a member employer's financial condition disqualifies it from corporation membership.

headings.title: Confidential board reports and solvency recommendations
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board by majority vote to make reports and recommendations to the division on member solvency, liquidation, rehabilitation, or conservation, exempting them from public document status.

headings.title: Board recommendations for insolvency detection and prevention
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board by majority vote to make recommendations to the division for detecting and preventing employer insolvencies.

headings.title: Post-insolvency report on history and cause
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board, at the conclusion of any member insolvency in which the corporation paid covered claims, to prepare and submit a report on the insolvency's history and cause to the division.

headings.title: Further recommendations under plan of operation
headings.reviewNote: Directs both the board and division to establish further recommendations as the occasion suggests under the section 287.870 plan of operation and applicable rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Mutual board and division duties to report hazardous financial conditions, board requests for qualification determinations, confidential solvency recommendations, and post-insolvency reports.

headings.title: Medical claims data reporting requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires licensed commercial workers' compensation insurers to submit electronic medical claims history data every six months subject to section 287.740 penalties, and permits division verification data collection from health care providers.

headings.title: Comparable data from consolidated health care plan
headings.reviewNote: Requires the Missouri consolidated health care plan established under section 103.005, upon division request, to provide data comparable to insurer reports under subsection 1.

headings.title: Cost trend analysis, availability, and patient anonymization
headings.reviewNote: Directs division use of reported data to analyze workers' compensation versus non-workers' compensation health care cost trends, makes data available to system users, legislators, and agencies, and bars identifying patients or providers.

headings.title: Workers' compensation fund payment for division costs
headings.reviewNote: Directs that any additional personnel or equipment needed by the division to meet section requirements be paid from the workers' compensation fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Semiannual commercial insurer medical claims data reporting, comparable data from the Missouri consolidated health care plan, anonymized trend analysis, and workers' compensation fund financing.

headings.title: Mandatory residual market plan of operation
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director within forty-five days of August 28, 1993, to approve a residual market plan of operation guaranteeing coverage and loss prevention services, beginning operation January 1, 1994.

headings.title: Insurer participation and equitable deficit sharing
headings.reviewNote: Requires all authorized workers' compensation insurers to participate and share losses.

headings.title: Filing disapproval, seventy-five-day review, and advisory filings
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to disapprove noncompliant filings, deems filings compliant unless acted upon within seventy-five days, applies voluntary market disapproval procedures, and permits the designated advisory organization to make filings.

headings.title: Service quality standards and in-state claims handling
headings.reviewNote: Directs rulemaking to ensure residual market employers receive voluntary-market service quality and insurer assignment rules, and requires application processing, loss control, and claims handling in Missouri or adjoining states.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishment of the workers' compensation residual market plan, mandatory insurer participation and deficit assessments, seventy-five-day filing review, and service quality standards.

headings.title: Definitions of company, department, and director
headings.reviewNote: Defines company, department, and director for purposes of converting an independent public workers' compensation corporation.

headings.title: Amended articles filing and January 1, 2025 conversion
headings.reviewNote: Permits filing amended articles before January 1, 2025, to convert into a chapter 379 private mutual insurance corporation, directing the director and secretary of state to issue amended certificates and reauthorize filings effective January 1, 2025.

headings.title: Continuation or change of corporate name
headings.reviewNote: Permits the company to continue conducting business under its existing name or adopt another name complying with state law.

headings.title: Succession to assets and state nonliability
headings.reviewNote: Makes the converted private mutual corporation successor in interest to all company assets and liabilities by operation of law from and after January 1, 2025, and disclaims state liability for corporate, company, or subsidiary debts.

entries.reviewSummary: Definitions, pre-2025 filing of amended articles to convert an independent public workers' compensation corporation into a chapter 379 private mutual insurance corporation, corporate name continuation, and asset succession with state nonliability.

headings.title: Payment of policyholder dividends permitted
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that sections 287.930 to 287.975 do not prohibit or regulate policyholder dividends, savings, or unabsorbed premium deposits, while prohibiting unfair discrimination between policyholders in paying them.

headings.title: Dividend plans excluded from rating systems
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a plan for paying dividends, savings, or unabsorbed premium deposits shall not be considered a rating plan or system.

headings.title: Unfair trade practice for renewal-conditioned dividends
headings.reviewNote: Declares it an unfair trade practice under sections 375.934 and 375.936 to condition payment of any dividend or portion thereof upon policy or contract renewal.

entries.reviewSummary: Permitted insurer payment of policyholder dividends without unfair discrimination, exclusion of dividend plans from rating plans, and prohibition on conditioning dividends on policy renewal.

headings.title: Prohibition against anti-competitive rate agreements
headings.reviewNote: Forbids insurers and advisory organizations from agreeing to fix rates or restrain trade.

headings.title: Prohibition on rate adherence agreements and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits insurers from agreeing with another insurer or the advisory organization to adhere to any rate, rating plan (other than the uniform experience rating plan), or rating rule except as needed to comply with section 287.955.

headings.title: Parallel use of rates insufficient for agreement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that consistent or intermittent use of the same rates, plans, schedules, rules, forms, classifications, or materials by two or more insurers is insufficient alone to support finding an agreement.

headings.title: Concerted action by commonly controlled insurers
headings.reviewNote: Permits two or more insurers under common ownership, management, or control to act in concert regarding activities authorized under sections 287.930 to 287.975 as a single insurer.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibitions on unreasonable trade restraints and rate adherence agreements except uniform experience rating, parallel conduct evidentiary rule, and concerted action among commonly controlled insurers.

headings.title: Examination of insurers and advisory organizations
headings.reviewNote: Permits the director to examine any insurer and the advisory organization as deemed necessary to ascertain compliance with sections 287.930 to 287.975.

headings.title: Access to books, records, and accounts
headings.reviewNote: Requires examined entities to provide reasonable access to books, accounts, and files.

headings.title: Payment of examination and audit costs
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that reasonable costs of examination shall be paid by the examined entity.

headings.title: Acceptance of out-of-state examination reports
headings.reviewNote: Permits director to accept examination reports from insurance supervisory officials of other states.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes regulatory examinations of insurers and advisory organizations, access to rating records, cost assessments, and audit report procedures.

headings.title: Administrative penalties for rating noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Permits the director to impose penalties up to one thousand dollars per violation of sections 287.930 to 287.975, or up to ten thousand dollars for willful violations, in addition to other legal penalties.

headings.title: Separate daily violation for using unfiled rates
headings.reviewNote: Deems an insurer using a rate without filing required rate, supplementary, or supporting information to commit a separate violation for each day the failure continues.

headings.title: Suspension or revocation of insurer license
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes suspension or revocation of certificate of authority or advisory license.

headings.title: Effective date and duration of license suspension
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to determine when a license suspension takes effect and its duration unless modified, rescinded, or the underlying order is modified, rescinded, or reversed.

headings.title: Issuance of formal order and findings
headings.reviewNote: Requires director to issue written findings and formal order following hearing.

entries.reviewSummary: Administrative monetary penalties for rating law violations, daily violations for unfiled rates, license suspension or revocation for order noncompliance, suspension duration, and written hearing order requirements.

headings.title: Presumption of competitive insurance market
headings.reviewNote: Establishes statutory presumption that a competitive market exists in workers' compensation insurance.

headings.title: Factors for determining reasonable degree of competition
headings.reviewNote: Lists seven mandatory economic factors, including workable competition tests, Herfindahl-Herschman Index concentration, insurer count, market shares, entry ease, and long-term profitability, to consider in determining competition.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes a statutory presumption of a competitive workers' compensation insurance market and specifies standards and hearing requirements for finding noncompetitive markets.

headings.title: Rate filing deadline in competitive markets
headings.reviewNote: Requires rate filing within thirty days after effective date in competitive markets.

headings.title: Prior rate filing in noncompetitive markets
headings.reviewNote: Requires prefiling thirty days prior to effective date if noncompetitive market found.

headings.title: Form of filings and incomplete filing notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires rate filings in the director's prescribed form and directs the director in noncompetitive markets to notify insurers within fifteen days of missing information before a filing is deemed made.

headings.title: Public inspection of rate filings
headings.reviewNote: Provides that all filed rate materials become open records available for public inspection.

entries.reviewSummary: Rate filing deadlines in competitive and noncompetitive insurance markets, filing form and incomplete-filing notice procedures, and public inspection access.

headings.title: Standards prohibiting excessive or inadequate rates
headings.reviewNote: Defines when insurance rates are considered excessive or inadequate under rating law.

headings.title: Standards prohibiting unfairly discriminatory rates
headings.reviewNote: Defines unfair discrimination based on loss and expense differentials between classifications.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines statutory standards prohibiting excessive, inadequate, or unfairly discriminatory workers' compensation insurance rates.

headings.title: Mandatory adherence to uniform classification and rating
headings.reviewNote: Requires every workers' compensation insurer to adhere to a uniform classification system and uniform experience rating plan filed by the designated advisory organization, subject to director disapproval.

headings.title: Insurer subclassifications, thirty-day filing, and disapproval
headings.reviewNote: Permits insurers to develop subclassifications filed thirty days before use, directing director disapproval if the insurer fails to show consistent data reporting.

headings.title: Advisory organization designation and insurer experience reporting
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to designate an advisory organization for statistical reporting and requires insurers to record and report experience under the approved uniform statistical plan.

headings.title: Advisory organization development of manual rules
headings.reviewNote: Directs the designated advisory organization to develop and file manual rules, subject to director approval, reasonably related to recording and reporting data.

headings.title: Adherence to manual rules and agreement restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurers to adhere to approved manual rules and the experience rating plan, and prohibits agreeing to adhere to manual rules not reasonably related to data recording and reporting.

headings.title: Individual risk premium modification plans and disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Permits insurers to file individual risk premium modification plans thirty days before use, caps schedule rating at plus or minus twenty-five percent (plus ten percent expense credit) and risk modeling at plus or minus fifty percent, and requires thirty-day disclosure to employers while protecting chapter 417 trade secrets.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory insurer adherence to uniform classification, experience rating, and manual rules, insurer subclassifications, advisory organization statistical reporting, and individual risk premium modification plans.

headings.title: Timing of rate disapproval and residual market approval
headings.reviewNote: Specifies when rates may be disapproved and requires prior approval for residual market rates.

headings.title: Disapproval standards for competitive and noncompetitive markets
headings.reviewNote: Permits the director to disapprove competitive-market rates found inadequate or unfairly discriminatory and requires disapproving noncompetitive-market rates found excessive, inadequate, or unfairly discriminatory under section 287.950.

headings.title: Supporting information and hearing in noncompetitive markets
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes requiring supporting rate filings and hearing when lack of competition found.

headings.title: Supporting rate information in competitive markets
headings.reviewNote: Permits requiring supporting rate information and calling a hearing prior to disapproval if competitive-market rates appear to violate section 287.950 or the act; source footnote notes 'this act' refers to S.B. 251, 1993.

headings.title: Disapproval of prefiled rates without hearing
headings.reviewNote: Allows disapproval of prefiled pending rates without hearing subject to insurer hearing request.

headings.title: Content and scope of rate disapproval orders
headings.reviewNote: Governs contents of disapproval orders, discontinuation dates, and premium adjustments.

headings.title: Establishment of interim rates and escrow accounts
headings.reviewNote: Provides for interim rates and premium escrow accounts pending final rate approval.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates director disapproval of workers' compensation insurance rates, hearing procedures, disapproval orders, interim rates, and premium escrow accounts.

headings.title: Hearing notice and location requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires at least thirty days' written notice and a director-designated location for hearings, a full stenographic record, optional hearing officer designation, and orders based on findings of fact and conclusions of law.

headings.title: Written findings, conclusions, and orders
headings.reviewNote: Requires written findings and conclusions issued within twenty days following hearing conclusion.

headings.title: Judicial review of administrative rate orders
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes insurers or the advisory organization to seek judicial declaratory relief on order validity without prior reconsideration, reviewed on the record and affirmed if supported by competent and substantial evidence.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes administrative hearing procedures for rate disapproval, written finding deadlines, and rights to judicial review.

headings.title: Application for hearing by aggrieved party
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes aggrieved persons or organizations to apply for administrative hearing on rate filings.

headings.title: Hearing findings and prospective disapproval order
headings.reviewNote: Governs issuance of disapproval order specifying future date when filing ceases to be effective.

entries.reviewSummary: Permits aggrieved parties to challenge effective rate filings, provides for administrative hearings, and regulates disapproval orders.

headings.title: Mandatory licensing for advisory rating organizations
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits providing rate services without obtaining advisory organization license from director.

headings.title: Non-discriminatory service to authorized insurers
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits advisory organization from refusing rating services to any authorized insurer.

headings.title: Application requirements for advisory license
headings.reviewNote: Details corporate documents, member lists, and process service designation required for license.

headings.title: Duty to report material application changes
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicant and licensee to promptly notify director of material changes in application facts.

headings.title: Issuance of license and advisory designation
headings.reviewNote: Governs issuance of advisory license and regulatory designation of advisory organization.

headings.title: Duration and validity of advisory license
headings.reviewNote: Provides that license remains effective until withdrawal, suspension, or revocation.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs mandatory licensing, application requirements, non-discriminatory service obligations, and regulatory designation of advisory rating organizations.

headings.title: Permitted advisory organization statistical activities
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates statutory powers of advisory organization including loss data collection and rating plans.

headings.title: Distribution and use of pure premium rate data
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes distribution and optional insurer use of pure premium data adjusted for loss development.

entries.reviewSummary: Enumerates permitted statistical, research, and rating services of advisory organizations, and authorizes distribution of adjusted pure premium rate data.

headings.title: Filing pure premium rates and rating schedules
headings.reviewNote: Requires advisory organization to file pure premium rates and rating manuals with director within thirty days.

headings.title: Construction payroll differential data and formula
headings.reviewNote: Directs data collection and formula development to equalize construction group premium rates.

headings.title: Construction rate equalization formula effective date
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes that the 1999 construction rate equalization formula shall be effective January 1, 2014.

headings.title: Quarterly payroll submission for contracting credit
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes construction employers to submit quarterly payroll data for contracting premium credit calculations.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates advisory organization filing of pure premium rates and rating schedules, construction payroll equalization formulas, and payroll credit submissions.
